registered: 2026-11-25, before the vortex lattice was run on this wing

source.reference: J. Zerihan, An Investigation into the Aerodynamics of Wings in Ground Effect, PhD thesis, University of Southampton, 2001 (supervisor X. Zhang); the single element wing of Zerihan & Zhang, J. Aircraft 37(6), 2000
source.wing: Tyrrell 026 front-wing main element, LS(1)-0413 MOD, chord 223.4 mm, span 1100 mm (AR 4.92), endplates 250 x 100 x 4 mm, moving ground, Re 0.43-0.46 million, transition free, reference incidence 1 deg (3.45 deg true); profile from the thesis's Table 2
source.height: h = ground to the lowest point of the suction surface

model: KinematiK's vortex lattice on the same profile and span, wing only: the endplates are not modelled (the lattice takes one lifting surface), and the flow is inviscid.
reported_not_graded: The maximum (1.72 at h/c 0.082) and the shape of the curve below h/c 0.3, where the measured downforce is limited by separation an inviscid model does not have.

phase_2.added: 2026-11-25, after the phase-1 run failed, when endplates were added to the lattice
phase_2.endplates: Modelled as flat vertical lifting surfaces at the wing tips. The thesis gives their size (250 x 100 x 4 mm) but not their placement or which side is vertical. Assumed: 250 mm long, centred on the chord, 100 mm tall, lower edge level with the wing's lowest point (the thesis says they were sized to allow very low ground heights). The other orientation (100 long, 250 tall, same lower edge) is reported as a bracket, not graded.
phase_2.graded: the same two points, the same 10 % limit
